Advisory.Description: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. SignalR connections are not consistently bound to the identity negotiated at connection establishment, allowing injected messages to execute Hub invocations as the victim. ## Announcement Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/504 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Critical - **Score:** 9.0 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-863 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The tables list affected version ranges and fixed package versions. Runtime and standalone deliveries are listed separately. ### ASP.NET Core 2.3 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- 11.0.0-preview.1.26104.118, <= 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.0 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Check the deployed runtime and application package versions against the affected ranges above. Self-contained applications include their own runtime; updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace it. ### How do I fix the issue? Install the applicable runtime or update each independently referenced package to the fixed version above. After updating standalone packages, rebuild and redeploy affected applications, including framework-dependent applications; restarting alone does not replace app-local packages. Restart applications. Rebuild and redeploy self-contained applications; updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace their embedded runtime. An SDK update alone does not update an application's standalone package references. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue.
